newsitem.title: USA: Help-wanted ad volume down in August.
newsitem.headline: Help-wanted ad volume down in August.

text.p: The volume of job advertisements in the United States edged lower in August but remained strong as the economy continued to expand, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
The private business group's U.S. help-wanted advertising index fell to 82.0 in August from 83.0 in July and August 1995.

In August, the volume of help-wanted advertising in 51 newspapers nationwide rose in seven of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increases were in the Middle Atlantic, Pacific, West North Central and East South Central regions, the Conference Board said.

"While the labour market continues to expand, although unevenly, latest data on want-ad volume shows no drop in the demand for labour," Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein said in a statement. "Given the high level of employment, there are no signs that job growth will slow.

"With the unemployment rate holding at or below 5.5 percent for 22 months, there's now a good chance that the umemployment rate will fall below 5 percent sometime in the first half of 1997," Goldstein said.

While the Midwestern and Mountain states have experienced a drop in job advertising volume during the last three months, there is enough strength in other labour markets to offset the weakness in these regions, the Conference Board said.
